title: Cliques in Hampton's band and his drinking buddies
summary: Hampton's band was a syndicate of groups; Cobb fell in with Milton Buckner, Jack McVea, Fred Beckett and Al Hayes, who were drinkers rather than users.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: How did you find Hamp's band? It wasn't a family band like the one you'd left, was it?

No, it wasn't the same thing because that was too much of a syndicated situation in that band, different groups for different things. You've got guys that groom together to do certain things that maybe I don't do. So I got with the guys that do the things I do, like Milton Buckner, Jack McVea, Fred Beckett, Al Hayes, about five of us and myself. And we got to be real buddies, but we were drinking buddies, you know. We didn't go the whole route.
And that was it. Milton Buckner worked for me on that band like he'd been knowing me for years, and I never met
him before in my life, and we stayed like that all the way until his death.

Well, Arnett, when you talk about, you know, you guys got your kicks from drinking and this made a clique in the band, in the same way people (inaudible) using different kinds of drugs, they had (inaudible). Now, it's just natural really, isn't it?
I guess. I don't know because I don't know. I haven't been on that side of the fence.
Well, I mean I'm sitting, you know, people like in Duke's band and several people were addicts, you know. They hung out together.
Birds of a feather flock together. But that wasn't my bag, so I had to go on my route. That's what I'm saying to you, you know.
